title: Enfield Emergency Help Points
summary: 24/7 emergency hospitals, urgent treatment centres, and local hazards across Enfield borough.
content:
For immediate life-threatening medical emergencies, always dial 999 first.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals with A&E
- North Middlesex University Hospital: Sterling Way, Edmonton, N18 1QX. From Silver Street station: ~5 min walk west along Sterling Way (A406 North Circular Road), or bus 34, 102, or 144.
- Barnet Hospital: Wellhouse Lane, Barnet, EN5 3DJ (serving western Enfield). From Enfield Town station: bus 307 heading west directly to hospital gates (~35 mins).
- Major Trauma Centre: The Royal London Hospital, Whitechapel Road, Whitechapel, E1 1FR. From Edmonton Green or Enfield Town: London Overground to Liverpool Street, then Elizabeth line or District line to Whitechapel.

2. Urgent Treatment Centres (Walk-In)
- North Middlesex Urgent Treatment Centre: Sterling Way, Edmonton, N18 1QX (located at hospital entrance). Open 24/7.
- Chase Farm Hospital Urgent Treatment Centre: The Ridgeway, Enfield, EN2 8JL. From Enfield Town station: ~25 min walk north-west up Enfield Chase and The Ridgeway, or take bus W8 or 313.

3. Local Area Hazard Notes
- River Lea and Lee Navigation: extensive flood risk zones across eastern Enfield, including Ponders End, Enfield Lock, and Edmonton Marshes.
- Tributary Brooks: Salmons Brook and Pymmes Brook carry fast-rising flash flood risks in central/southern Edmonton during heavy rain.

4. Essential Supplies During Outages
Pharmacies and supermarkets in Enfield Town (Church Street and Palace Gardens), Edmonton Green Shopping Centre, and Green Lanes (Palmers Green) can supply drinking water, hygiene items, and emergency medicines.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
